name: Bill Hagerty
bio: Former U.S. Ambassador to Japan and Tennessee Commissioner of Economic and Community Development. Trump-endorsed; $5.3M cash on hand.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Sen. Hagerty has not publicly championed expanded federal investment in early childhood education or childcare. He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act which contained tax provisions but no new childcare funding or Head Start expansions.
early_childhood_ed.details: No public statements from Hagerty specifically promoting pre-K access, Head Start funding, childcare subsidies, or early learning programs were found as of July 2026. Hagerty voted 'Yes' on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on July 1, 2025, which he championed as providing historic tax relief to families. On the 2024 Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act (H.R. 7024), which included a modest Child Tax Credit expansion, Hagerty voted against cloture, aligning with most Senate Republicans. No evidence was found that Hagerty cosponsored the 'Building Child Care for a Better Future Act' (2025), a Democratic-led bill to expand childcare funding. Hagerty did not participate in Knox News voter's guide interviews for the 2026 Senate race.

child_hunger.summary: Sen. Hagerty voted 'Yes' on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 2025), which cut approximately $186 billion from SNAP and added new work requirements. About 100,000 Tennesseans subsequently lost food assistance. Hagerty publicly championed the bill but did not address the SNAP reductions specifically for children.
child_hunger.details: On July 1, 2025, Hagerty voted in favor of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which he described publicly as 'a once-in-a-generation opportunity.' The law included approximately $186 billion in SNAP cuts, new work requirements removing prior exemptions for people over 55, veterans, and homeless individuals, and shifted SNAP benefit costs to states. By June 2026, about 100,000 Tennesseans had lost food benefits since the law took effect in July 2025. Tennessee counties were estimated to lose a net $5.3 billion in federal help over 10 years under the SNAP cuts. Advocacy groups held demonstrations outside Hagerty's Nashville office urging him to reject SNAP cuts before the Senate vote. Hagerty has not issued public statements specifically addressing the impact on child hunger in Tennessee as a result of these cuts.

parental_support.summary: Hagerty supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which he says includes the 'largest tax cut for American families in our nation's history,' but independent analysts found it would block up to 20 million children in lower-income working families from the full $2,500 Child Tax Credit. He voted against the 2024 bipartisan Child Tax Credit expansion bill.
parental_support.details: Hagerty was a leading Senate advocate for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, claiming a family of four could see approximately $10,900 more per year. However, the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities and CNBC reported that the bill's Child Tax Credit structure would block approximately 20 million children in working families from receiving the full $2,500 credit because their parents do not earn enough income. In 2024, Hagerty voted against cloture on H.R. 7024 (Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act), which contained a bipartisan Child Tax Credit expansion estimated to benefit 16 million children in poverty or near poverty. No public statements by Hagerty supporting paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or other direct parental support programs were found as of July 2026.

name: Marquita Bradshaw
bio: Memphis environmental justice activist who won the 2020 Democratic primary against expectations. Running again on environmental and economic-justice platform.
photo_credit: Bradshaw for Senate official campaign website

early_childhood_ed.summary: Marquita Bradshaw has consistently supported universal pre-K and quality childcare access as part of her platform across her 2020 and 2026 Senate campaigns. She supports funding public education 'the same as we do our military.'
early_childhood_ed.details: Bradshaw's campaign website states 'I BELIEVE IN HIGH QUALITY PUBLIC EDUCATION' and she has previously called for 'Fund universal pre-K education' and 'Provide quality childcare' as explicit policy goals in her 2020 campaign platform. She has also stated a key campaign message is 'High quality public education pre-k-12 that prepare students for success in higher education and workforce.' Bradshaw opposes school vouchers, strongly favoring public school investment. Her campaign website for the 2026 race maintains her belief in high-quality public education funding.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public statements by Marquita Bradshaw on SNAP, school meals, WIC, or child hunger programs were found as of July 2026. Her campaign platform emphasizes economic affordability and a living wage, which she frames as connected to family food security.
child_hunger.details: No public statements or campaign materials from Bradshaw's 2026 Senate campaign specifically address SNAP, school meal programs, WIC, food banks, or summer food programs for children. Her campaign platform includes a call for raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour and building 'an economy that helps all Tennesseans.' In July 2026 voter's guide interviews, she discussed affordability broadly but did not specify child nutrition programs. No public statements on the One Big Beautiful Bill's SNAP cuts were found directly attributed to Bradshaw.

parental_support.summary: Bradshaw supports a living wage of at least $15 per hour as a core form of economic support for families, and has supported healthcare for all and public education funding as family-support measures. No specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit expansions, or childcare subsidies were found in her 2026 campaign materials.
parental_support.details: Bradshaw's campaign platform includes a call to raise the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour immediately. She also supports Medicare for All as a healthcare platform. Bradshaw is a single mother who raised her son on a working-class salary, and her biography notes this experience shapes her economic advocacy. Her 2020 campaign platform included support for 'quality childcare' and 'universal pre-K.' No specific 2026 statements on paid family leave, the Child Tax Credit, childcare subsidies, or maternal health policy were found.

name: Maria Brewer
bio: Longtime Tennessee Democratic Party staffer making her first run for federal office.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Maria Brewer has expressed support for investing in quality public schools and stated that 'our children deserve the education needed to earn good American wages and benefits,' but no specific positions on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare programs were found in her 2026 campaign materials.
early_childhood_ed.details: Brewer's 2026 U.S. Senate campaign website focuses on grassroots organizing and corruption accountability but does not include a detailed policy platform on early childhood education or childcare. In a 2026 podcast appearance, Brewer discussed healthcare, motherhood, and cost-of-living as campaign motivations, but no specific early childhood education policy was articulated. The Tennessee Lookout voter profile describes her issues as 'protecting Social Security and Medicare from cuts, raising the minimum wage and making college and vocational education available and affordable' — suggesting her education focus is on higher/vocational rather than early childhood.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public positions by Maria Brewer on SNAP, school meals, child nutrition programs, or summer food assistance were found as of July 2026.
child_hunger.details: Brewer's 2026 campaign materials do not specifically address child hunger, SNAP, WIC, school meal programs, or summer food assistance for children. In voter's guide interviews, she addressed high grocery costs in the context of tariff policy and corporate competition, stating 'we need to level the playing field for small business owners by cutting out the subsidies to big corporations and let increased competition bring down prices.' She criticized the Big Beautiful Bill and its champions for being 'disconnected from the experiences of everyday Tennesseans.' However, she did not specifically reference SNAP, food banks, or child nutrition programs.

parental_support.summary: Maria Brewer has cited personal experience with healthcare costs and motherhood as motivating her Senate campaign, and she supports protecting Social Security and Medicare and raising the minimum wage. No specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, or childcare subsidies were found in her 2026 campaign materials.
parental_support.details: In her April 2026 podcast appearance, Brewer described 'campaign motivations rooted in ordinary working-family experience, healthcare and motherhood' and emphasized high cost of living. Her documented 2026 campaign priorities include protecting Social Security and Medicare from cuts, raising the minimum wage, and making college and vocational education affordable. No specific statements on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit expansions, childcare subsidies, or maternal health policy were found in her 2026 materials.
